subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when configured, or keep the shipped host-local/TZ behavior?
rationale: Current main has split behavior: auto-flush uses configured timezone, while session-memory artifacts ship as host-local; changing filenames and headers affects existing artifact conventions and needs maintainer intent before automation changes it.

options.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Change bundled session-memory to resolve `agents.defaults.userTimezone`, update tests and docs, and keep the existing config surface unchanged.

options.title: Keep host-local artifacts
options.body: Document session-memory artifact naming as host-local/TZ behavior and close this issue as not planned.

options.title: Add explicit memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory-artifact timezone option, accepting the schema, docs, migration, and support burden of new config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Change bundled session-memory to resolve `agents.defaults.userTimezone`, update tests and docs, and keep the existing config surface unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits at the memory/time/config product boundary, and this person has recent history in the configured-timezone and memory-core surfaces.
